BET 2026 Diagnostic model

BET 2026 Diagnostic model: self-test

Self-test methods and interpretation

  • Operating model. The fitted final parameter state of the Diagnostic model was treated as the generating truth for pseudo-data generation and recovery comparisons. The negative-binomial tag overdispersion parameter τ was fixed at 2 in the generating model and in every refit.
  • Simulation and refitting. 50 independent pseudo-data sets were generated with replicate-specific seeds. CPUE, length-composition, age-at-length and post-mixing tag observations were simulated; catch and empirical pre-mixing tag observations remained conditioned. Each data set was refitted with the recorded MFCL doitall schedule, and figures include refits meeting the archived MGC criterion (1.0e-04). All 50 refits met this criterion.
  • Purpose and scope. This model-consistent simulation-estimation test evaluates internal consistency and practical estimability under the configured observation models. It can reveal finite-sample recovery problems, including weak identification that may be masked by influential observations in the fitted data. Such recovery problems can be consistent with reliance on observations that are atypical under the assumed likelihood, but confirming a distributional mismatch requires comparison of observed residual or influence statistics with their pseudo-data distributions. The test does not determine whether the fitted generating values are unbiased estimates of the unknown population.
  • Recovery targets. Annual depletion (SB/SBF=0), spawning potential (SB), no-fishing spawning potential (SBF=0), recruitment (R) and annual fishing mortality (F) are compared with their generating truth. Recent summaries use the MFCL windows read from the model: SBrecent T-3 to T; SBF=0 T-10 to T-1; annual-F diagnostic T-4 to T-1. Native MSY quantities are read directly from MFCL output, with equilibrium spawning biomass at MSY denoted SBMSY. Parameter recovery is restricted to Recruitment scale (ln R0), Stock-recruitment density-dependence coefficient, Mean length at youngest age (L1), Mean length at oldest age (L2), von Bertalanffy growth coefficient (K), Length-at-age SD scale (s1), Age-related trend in length-at-age SD (s2).
  • Recovery summaries. For each replicate, period-average relative error is calculated against the corresponding operating-model quantity. Figures show the empirical distributions across the refits; these are diagnostic distributions, not parameter confidence intervals.
  • Reporting basis. The simulation-estimation design follows the self-test framework described by Deroba et al. (2015), while the interpretation of observation-error variance and practical estimability follows Kim et al. (2024). Reporting follows the WCPO bigeye assessment focus used by Day et al. (2023, WCPFC-SC19-SA-WP-05) and the stock-status quantities identified for the 2026 SC22 review.
er,X = 100 × (Xrefitr − Xtruth) / |Xtruth|

Here, r indexes a self-test replicate, X is an assessment quantity or selected estimated parameter, and the overbar denotes the mean over the model-specific recent period when a period average is reported. Relative RMSE is √[meanr(er,X2)].

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{Operating model.} The fitted final parameter state of the Diagnostic model was treated as the generating truth for pseudo-data generation and recovery comparisons. The negative-binomial tag overdispersion parameter τ was fixed at 2 in the generating model and in every refit.
\item \textbf{Simulation and refitting.} 50 independent pseudo-data sets were generated with replicate-specific seeds. CPUE, length-composition, age-at-length and post-mixing tag observations were simulated; catch and empirical pre-mixing tag observations remained conditioned. Each data set was refitted with the recorded MFCL doitall schedule, and figures include refits meeting the archived MGC criterion (1.0e-04). All 50 refits met this criterion.
\item \textbf{Purpose and scope.} This model-consistent simulation-estimation test evaluates internal consistency and practical estimability under the configured observation models. It can reveal finite-sample recovery problems, including weak identification that may be masked by influential observations in the fitted data. Such recovery problems can be consistent with reliance on observations that are atypical under the assumed likelihood, but confirming a distributional mismatch requires comparison of observed residual or influence statistics with their pseudo-data distributions. The test does not determine whether the fitted generating values are unbiased estimates of the unknown population.
\item \textbf{Recovery targets.} Annual depletion ($\mathrm{SB}/\mathrm{SB}_{F=0}$), spawning potential (SB), no-fishing spawning potential ($\mathrm{SB}_{F=0}$), recruitment (R) and annual fishing mortality (F) are compared with their generating truth. Recent summaries use the MFCL windows read from the model: $\mathrm{SB}_{\mathrm{recent}}$ T-3 to T; $\mathrm{SB}_{F=0}$ T-10 to T-1; annual-F diagnostic T-4 to T-1. Native MSY quantities are read directly from MFCL output, with equilibrium spawning biomass at MSY denoted $\mathrm{SB}_{\mathrm{MSY}}$. Parameter recovery is restricted to Recruitment scale ($\ln R_0$), Stock-recruitment density-dependence coefficient, Mean length at youngest age ($L_1$), Mean length at oldest age ($L_2$), von Bertalanffy growth coefficient ($K$), Length-at-age SD scale ($s_1$), Age-related trend in length-at-age SD ($s_2$).
\item \textbf{Recovery summaries.} For each replicate, period-average relative error is calculated against the corresponding operating-model quantity. Figures show the empirical distributions across the refits; these are diagnostic distributions, not parameter confidence intervals.
\item \textbf{Reporting basis.} The simulation-estimation design follows the self-test framework described by Deroba et al. (2015), while the interpretation of observation-error variance and practical estimability follows Kim et al. (2024). Reporting follows the WCPO bigeye assessment focus used by Day et al. (2023, WCPFC-SC19-SA-WP-05) and the stock-status quantities identified for the 2026 SC22 review.
\end{itemize}
\[
e_{r,X}=100\,\frac{\overline{X}^{\mathrm{refit}}_{r}-\overline{X}^{\mathrm{truth}}}{\left|\overline{X}^{\mathrm{truth}}\right|},
\qquad
\mathrm{RRMSE}_{X}=\sqrt{\frac{1}{n}\sum_{r=1}^{n} e_{r,X}^{2}}.
\]
Here, $r$ indexes a self-test replicate, $X$ is an assessment quantity or selected estimated parameter, and the overbar denotes the mean over the model-specific recent period when a period average is reported.

Results

Diagnostic model. 50 of 50 pseudo-data refits completed and met the recorded convergence criterion. MGC ranged from 5.13e-05 to 9.97e-05. Median whole-series pseudo-data errors ranged from -0.23% to 0.07%. The generating truth was inside the pointwise central 95% empirical refit range at 385 of 438 annual quantity-year points (87.9%). Median relative bias across recent and native assessment summaries ranged from -2.1% to 3.5%. Across the selected recruitment-scale, growth and stock-recruit parameters, median relative errors ranged from -3.85% to 2.00%. These are empirical simulation-estimation diagnostics under the configured generator, not confidence intervals for the assessment.

Key recovery

\caption{Relative recovery error for recent management and assessment quantities ending in 2024 and for selected estimated parameters in the Diagnostic model. Points are pseudo-data refits, boxes show their empirical distributions, and the red line marks exact recovery. Grey dashed lines mark relative recovery errors of -5\% and +5\%.}
